question: How many shares of common stock were outstanding as of the cover-page reference date?
rationale: After inspecting 5 representative cover pages, two layout families emerged: 7 docs embed the share count inside an 'outstanding' sentence on pages 1-3, while 3 docs (AMAZON 2016/2018, NIKE) put a label-only span on the cover page and the numeric value in a separate numeric-only span. R1 (rule_cover_outstanding_label) catches the sentence/label in all 10 docs. R2 (rule_cover_numeric_value) catches numeric-only cover-page spans with >=2 thousand-separator groups, restricted to values <= 5e9 so that aggregate-market-value figures (which run to 10s-100s of billions) are excluded — this was critical for NIKE, whose multi-class table otherwise tempts the QA into the $180B market-value total. A third share-class context rule was tried but proved unnecessary once the numeric threshold filtered the market-value distractors; it was dropped. Final R: 2 rules, sum_cost 0.000454, union match_rate 1.0.
